1  [By Sri.Praveen Kumar.A .. Advocates]
 JUDGMENT

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Inspector of Nandini Layout police station against the accused no.1 to 4 for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 498A and 323 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that the accused no.1 married C.W.1- on 27.01.2023 at T.K.Hall at Yeshwanthpura, after marriage while C.W.1 was staying with the accused no.1 to 4 at the matrimonial house, the accused No.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention used extend physical and mental cruelty towards C.W.1 for petty reasons and the accused no.1 objected her mother and brother coming to his house and assaulted C.W.1 and caused hurt to her, therefore the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused no.1 to 4 before the Nandini Layout Police seeking necessary action against them in accordance with law.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No. 326/2023 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently C.C.1045/2024 who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn,
after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused no.1 to 4 , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offences.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, subsequently in persuance of summons the accused no.1 to 4 appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused no.1 to 4 , therefore charge was framed for the offences punishable U/Sec. 498A, 323 r/w Sec. 34 of IPC and read over and explained to the accused No.1 to 4 in the language known to them, after understanding the same they denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5. In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked two documents at Ex.P-1 and 2.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 11 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points C.C.1045/2024 that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1.

Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt the accused no.1 married C.W.1- on 27.01.2013 at T.K.Hall at Yeshwanthpura, after marriage while C.W.1 was staying with the accused no.1 to 4 at the matrimonial house, the accused No.1 to 4 with an intention to commit an offence and in furtherance of their common intention used extend physical and mental cruelty towards C.W.1 for petty reasons and thereby the accused no.1 to 4 have committed an offence of extending cruelty towards C.W.1, punishable under section 498A r/w Sec. 34 of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution further proves beyond all reasonable doubt that while C.W.1 was residing with the accused No.1 to 4 at the matrimonial home, the accused no.1 objected her mother and brother coming to his house and assaulted C.W.1 and caused hurt to her and thereby the accused no.1 has committed an offence of "voluntarily causing hurt"punishable U/s 323 of IPC?
3.. What Order?
8.

My answers to the above points are as under:
Point Nos.1 and 2 : in the 'Negative' Point No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Point No.1 and 2: These points are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid the repetation of facts.
10.

In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked two documents on her C.C.1045/2024 behalf as Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Dilshad Banu and she deposed in her evidence that accused No.1 is her husband, accused no.2 to 4 are mother, sister in law and brother of accused no.1, and her marriage was solemnized with the accused No.1 on 27.01.2013 at Bengaluru.
Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused No.1 she was residing at the matrimonial house with the accused and they were living with together.
Further she deposed that the accused did not extend mental and physical cruelty towards her and did not assault her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to Nandini Layout PS in the year 2023 police took her Nandinilayout Police Station vs Mohammed Jaffer on 26 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118774811/
3 signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence as per Ex.P.2.

sentences.text:
She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 and 2 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court,
cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence two documents got marked as Ex.P1 and P.2.
So far as Ex.P1 is the complaint and Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, but the C.C.1045/2024 prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same

,
therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused no.1 to 4 however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 , for which this Court is of the considered opinion that prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.1 to 4 beyond all reasonable doubt.

Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused no.1 to 4 ,
for which I answer point Nos.1and 2 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.3:

In view of my findings on point Nos.1 and 2 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused no.1 to 4 are not found guilty and they are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498A and 323 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 to 4 stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused no.1 to 4 are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal C.C.1045/2024 [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 26th day of December, 2025.)
(KESHAVA.K) XXXII Addl.
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru.
